value.rationale: The quantitative failure of energy passivity to guarantee equilibrium relaxation is an intrinsic design boundary for port-Hamiltonian splitting. Complete sharp stability sets, a parameter-explicit narrow fast-rate phase plateau and distinct asymptotic spectral versus per-step norm deficits inform natural step selection and long-time reliability. These go beyond a routine normalization or isolated negative check, while scope is restricted to a natural minimal oscillator.
